Curvature of the LPPLS objective at the estimate

Source: R/lppls_fitter.R
lppls_curvature.Rd

Tests whether the calibration sits at a genuine interior minimum.

Usage

lppls_curvature(x, log_price = NULL)

Arguments

x

An object of class "lppls_fit" from fit_lppls().

log_price

Optional numeric vector, the series the fit was calibrated on. Only needed for fits made before fit_lppls() stored it.

Value

An object of class "lppls_curvature": a list with the full and profile determinants, the profile Hessian and its eigenvalues, the active bounds, and a classification of "minimum", "saddle" or "maximum".

Details

The modified profile likelihood assumes the estimate is an interior minimum: its correction uses \(\det(X'X - H)\), the observed information, which is only guaranteed positive at an interior stationary point. \(X\) holds the model's first derivatives with respect to the six parameters, and \(H\) its second derivatives, each weighted by the residual at that observation and summed (thesis eq. 55). \(H\) is thus a residual-weighted curvature term rather than a Hessian in its own right. lppls_curvature() tests the determinant directly, and factorises it to show where the sign comes from.

By the Schur complement, \(\det(X'X - H)\) factorises into the determinant of the linear-parameter block times the determinant of the \(2 \times 2\) Hessian of the \((m, \omega)\) profile. The model is linear in \(A, B, C_1, C_2\), so their second derivatives vanish, \(H\) contributes nothing to the linear block, and what remains there is a crossproduct with a positive determinant. The sign is therefore decided entirely by curvature in the two nonlinear parameters: the \(2 \times 2\) block the function reports.

See also

fit_lppls(), print.lppls_fit()
